elements.element: Customer has no contractual restriction on soliciting Vendor personnel.
elements.evidence: Section 12.4 expressly prohibits Customer from soliciting persons employed by Vendor.

elements.element: Customer is prohibited from soliciting Vendor personnel.
elements.evidence: Section 12.4 states that Customer will not solicit persons employed by Vendor.

elements.element: Vendor is prohibited from soliciting Customer personnel.
elements.evidence: Section 12.5 subjects Vendor to the same restriction with respect to Customer's personnel.

elements.element: Each Party's restriction is limited to personnel directly involved in the Services.
elements.evidence: Although Section 12.5 refers to personnel directly involved in the Services, Section 12.4 separately prohibits Customer from soliciting any person employed by Vendor at any time. Section 12.5 does not expressly narrow or replace that broader covenant.

elements.element: The non-solicit duration is limited to 12 months.
The 12-month period runs from the end of the relevant person's involvement in the Services.
elements.evidence: Section 12.5 provides that the restriction applies in each case only for 12 months from the end of that person's involvement in the Services.

elements.element: The restriction does not apply to responses to general advertisements not targeted at the other Party's personnel.
elements.evidence: The final sentence of Section 12.5 contains this express carve-out and applies it to both Sections 12.4 and 12.5.

elements.element: The restriction does not apply where the person makes an unsolicited approach.
elements.evidence: The final sentence of Section 12.5 expressly excludes persons who make an unsolicited approach.

elements.element: The clause does not prohibit hiring or engaging personnel independently of solicitation.
elements.evidence: The operative restriction covers solicitation only, the prior prohibition on engaging personnel was removed, and Section 12.3 confirms that Customer made no no-hire commitment.

result.reason: The redline does not achieve the preferred position because Customer remains subject to a non-solicit. It also falls short of the fallback because Section 12.4 continues to cover any Vendor employee, while Section 12.5 describes a direct-involvement limitation without expressly applying that limitation to or superseding Section 12.4. This creates conflicting scope language and leaves Customer exposed to a broader restriction than the intended mutual fallback.
